title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court and the China Disabled Persons' Federation on Issuing the Ten Opinions on Providing Better Litigation Services for Persons with Disabilities
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court, China Disabled Persons' Federation

Notice on Issuing the Ten Opinions on Providing Better Quality Litigation Services for Persons with Disabilities

Fa [2024] No. 40

The high people's courts and disabled persons' federations of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; and the Disabled Persons' Federation of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

The Ten Opinions of the Supreme People's Court and the China Disabled Persons' Federation on Providing Better Quality Litigation Services for Persons with Disabilities are hereby issued for your conscientious implementation. Please accelerate the construction of barrier-free environments in litigation service centers to better safeguard the lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities. Major issues encountered during implementation shall be reported separately to the Supreme People's Court and the China Disabled Persons' Federation.

February 26, 2024

Supreme People's Court, China Disabled Persons' Federation

Ten Opinions on Providing Better Quality Litigation Services for Persons with Disabilities

To earnestly implement the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Persons with Disabilities and the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Construction of Accessible Environments, to promote litigation service work with the judicial philosophy of active justice in the new era, to effectively ensure that persons with disabilities participate in litigation activities equally, fully, and conveniently, to enhance the law-based level of preventing and resolving disputes involving persons with disabilities, and to better safeguard the lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities, the following opinions are put forward regarding the provision of better quality litigation services for persons with disabilities.

1. Improving the Construction of Accessible Facilities. Litigation service venues and service facilities newly built by people's courts at all levels shall comply with the Specifications for Accessible Environment Construction in Litigation Service Centers of People's Courts (see the Appendix). Where existing litigation service venues and service facilities do not meet the above construction specifications, necessary modifications shall be made. People's courts with the conditions are encouraged to build specialized accessible courtrooms and accessible mediation rooms. Local disabled persons' federations shall provide assistance and support for the construction and modification of accessible facilities in people's courts.

2. Strengthening Accessible Information Exchange. People's courts at all levels shall provide accessible information exchange services in litigation service venues for persons with disabilities of different categories, such as voice, large print, and synchronized subtitles. The accessible construction of platforms such as the online service of people's courts shall be strengthened to gradually comply with accessible website design standards and national information accessibility standards, making it more convenient for persons with disabilities to handle litigation matters online throughout the entire process. Local disabled persons' federations shall assist people's courts in establishing a roster of litigation assistance service personnel to facilitate the courts in contacting and scheduling professionals to provide litigation assistance services such as Braille and sign language interpretation.

3. Providing Refined Litigation Services. People's courts at all levels rely on the "hall, online, hotline, circuit" litigation service channels to provide refined litigation services for persons with disabilities. For those who can handle litigation matters independently on-site, they shall be guided to the green service window, where staff shall communicate patiently and guide them through the process; for those who cannot handle matters independently on-site, special personnel shall be arranged to provide agency or assistance services; for those who cannot come to the court to handle matters, persons with disabilities shall be guided to use convenient means such as the online service platform of people's courts or the 12368 litigation service hotline, or services such as appointment filing and door-to-door filing shall be provided. Judicial aid such as deferred, reduced, or exempted litigation costs shall be provided to eligible persons with disabilities in accordance with the law.

4. Fully Safeguarding the Litigation Rights of Persons with Disabilities. People's courts at all levels shall ensure that cases involving persons with disabilities are filed promptly in accordance with the law, and for lawsuits that meet the acceptance conditions, the principle of "every case must be filed, every lawsuit must be accepted" shall be followed. People's courts with conditions are encouraged to open green channels, specially mark cases involving persons with disabilities, and achieve priority in filing, trial, and enforcement. For cases eligible for small claims procedure, supervision procedure, or summary procedure, on the basis of fully respecting the wishes of the parties with disabilities, the cases shall be properly triaged by complexity to effectively improve the quality and efficiency of trials and ensure the prompt realization of the lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities.

5. Establishing a "General-to-General" Online Diversified Dispute Resolution Mechanism. The Supreme People's Court, together with the China Disabled Persons' Federation, shall establish a "general-to-general" online diversified dispute resolution mechanism. Local people's courts shall invite staff from disabled persons' federations and other organizations or individuals that meet the conditions and are willing to participate in the mediation of disputes involving persons with disabilities to join the mediation platform of people's courts and conduct mediation of disputes involving persons with disabilities individually or jointly.

6. Innovating Mediation and Resolution Models. Local people's courts may, together with disabled persons' federations, set up mediation studios or litigation service stations, where judges and staff from disabled persons' federations, among others, conduct legal consultations, litigation guidance, mediation, and resolution through a combination of online and offline methods. For disputes involving disabilities caused by traffic accidents, work-related injuries, medical incidents, etc., circuit trial points may be established at departments such as traffic management authorities, labor and social security departments, and health departments to jointly resolve disputes locally.

7. Establishing a Joint Resolution Mechanism for Petition Cases Involving Laws and Lawsuits. Disabled persons' federations shall regularly review and analyze petition cases involving laws and lawsuits reported by persons with disabilities. For petition cases with certain reasonableness, the principle of prioritizing mediation and separating petitions from lawsuits shall be followed to actively guide persons with disabilities to resolve disputes before litigation. For matters that cannot be resolved through mediation and fall within the acceptance scope of people's courts, assistance shall be provided to persons with disabilities to apply to the people's court with jurisdiction for resolution in accordance with the law. The disabled persons' federation at the place where the person with a disability resides shall provide support for the person's settlement, mediation, and litigation in local and non-local people's courts, promoting the substantive resolution of disputes.

8. Implementing Source Governance of Litigation. People's courts and disabled persons' federations at all levels shall proactively integrate into the pattern of source governance of litigation led by Party committees and dominated by governments, and work together to "grasp the front end and treat diseases before they occur." When resolving disputes, mediating, or providing litigation services, if people's courts at all levels discover that relevant units have not properly safeguarded the rights and interests of persons with disabilities or have infringed upon their lawful rights and interests, they shall promptly report to the local government's competent departments and disabled persons' federations, and if necessary, issue judicial suggestions to the unit, proposing targeted governance recommendations to prevent and reduce disputes involving persons with disabilities at the source.

9. Strengthening Joint Legal Publicity. People's courts and disabled persons' federations at all levels shall, based on the characteristics and needs of persons with disabilities, innovate forms of legal publicity, produce legal publicity products, and jointly carry out work such as explaining the law through cases and legal publicity, actively guiding persons with disabilities to respect, study, abide by, and use the law, enhance their legal awareness, and improve their ability to resolve disputes using legal thinking and legal methods.

10. Establishing a Communication and Coordination Mechanism. People's courts and disabled persons' federations at all levels shall strengthen communication and coordination, regularly exchange and discuss the implementation of these opinions in various regions, jointly coordinate and resolve difficulties and problems in the promotion process, and through means such as regular situation briefings, data and information sharing, joint meetings, joint research, and publication of typical cases, continuously enhance the capacity and level of litigation services.

Appendix: Specifications for Accessible Environment Construction in Litigation Service Centers of People's Courts

Appendix

Specifications for Accessible Environment Construction in Litigation Service Centers of People's Courts

1. Purpose

To promote the standardization, normalization, and humanization of accessible environment construction in litigation service centers of courts nationwide, and to comprehensively enhance the level of accessible environment construction in litigation service centers of people's courts, these specifications are formulated.

2. Definition

Accessible environment construction in litigation service centers refers to the provision of convenience for persons with disabilities, elderly persons, and other groups to independently and safely enter, exit, and pass through the litigation service center, use auxiliary facilities, obtain, use, and exchange information, and receive litigation services.

3. Scope of Application

These specifications constitute the unified standard for the construction of accessible environments in litigation service centers of courts nationwide and apply to new construction, renovation, and expansion projects of litigation service centers in people's courts.

The modification of existing litigation service venues shall be carried out with reference to these specifications.

4. Reference to Normative Documents

Law of the People's Republic of China on the Construction of Accessible Environments

Regulations on the Construction of Accessible Environments

Opinions of the Supreme People's Court and the China Disabled Persons' Federation on Effectively Safeguarding the Lawful Rights and Interests of Persons with Disabilities in Trial and Enforcement Work

Opinions of the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of Justice, and the China Disabled Persons' Federation on Deeply Studying and Implementing Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law and Effectively Strengthening Judicial Protection for Persons with Disabilities

5. Construction Principles

The construction of accessible environments in litigation service centers of people's courts shall be based on the principle of meeting the litigation service needs of persons with disabilities, adhere to proceeding from reality, and achieve adaptation to local conditions and functional applicability.

6. Accessible Passage Facilities

Litigation service centers shall be equipped with the following accessible passage facilities:

(1) The litigation service center shall be equipped with accessible entrances and exits and accessible passages to facilitate the entry and exit of persons with disabilities. Where there is a height difference on the ground of the accessible passage, a wheelchair ramp or curb ramp shall be provided.

(2) Where the litigation service center is located on the second floor or above of a building, accessible stairs or an accessible elevator shall be provided.

(3) Where public braille paths are provided at the entrance and exit of the litigation service center, outdoor braille paths shall be set up, and the outdoor braille paths shall be connected to the public braille paths.

(4) Where a parking lot is provided at the litigation service center, at least one accessible motor vehicle parking space shall be provided.

7. Accessible Service Facilities

Litigation service centers shall be equipped with the following accessible service facilities:

(1) Low-level service facilities, including low-level guidance counters, low-level service windows, low-level self-service equipment, etc.

(2) Toilets meeting accessibility requirements, or at least one accessible toilet stall in each of the men's and women's restrooms that are convenient for persons with disabilities to enter and exit.

(3) Wheelchair seating may be provided in areas such as the litigation service hall, mediation rooms, and courtrooms based on the actual site and use.

8. Accessible Signage

Accessible signage and text descriptions shall be provided at all accessible facilities in the litigation service center.

9. Accessible Assistive Devices

Litigation service centers shall, based on actual conditions, equip the following accessible assistive devices for persons with disabilities of different categories and degrees:

(1) Provide mobility assistive devices such as crutches and wheelchairs for persons with physical disabilities.

(2) Provide visual assistive devices such as magnifying glasses for persons with visual disabilities.

(3) Provide hearing assistive devices such as wireless hearing assistance systems for persons with hearing disabilities.

(4) Provide information communication assistive devices such as writing boards for persons with speech disabilities.

10. Accessible Litigation Materials

Litigation service centers shall, based on actual conditions, provide accessible versions of litigation materials in formats such as audio, large print, electronic, and Braille, including pre-litigation mediation guides, filing, responding to lawsuits, enforcement application instructions, and manuals for platforms such as the online service of people's courts:

(1) Where litigation materials are provided in paper form, the font size shall be no smaller than small three, with appropriate line spacing to facilitate identification and use by persons with disabilities.

(2) Where litigation materials are provided in electronic form, they shall have functions such as voice recognition and page font enlargement or reduction.

(3) Where litigation materials are provided in Braille form, they shall comply with the specifications of the National General Braille Scheme.

11. Personnel Training and Management

People's courts shall promote the use of accessible service manuals formulated by disabled persons' federations and their specialized associations in litigation service centers, strengthen the training and assessment of litigation service personnel, filing personnel, and court mediators, and further improve the level of accessible services in people's courts.

12. Construction Standards

The construction of accessible environments in litigation service centers shall comply with the provisions of national accessible environment construction standards such as the General Code for Accessibility of Buildings and Municipal Engineering (GB 55019-2021).
